item.description:
### Fixed - **A missed file event can no longer freeze a session's status until you relaunch.** Hook-driven sessions reach Perch through a directory watch, and that watch was the only path. Every scan now also checks whether the directory changed and reloads if the watch missed it, so a stuck status is caught within a few seconds instead of never. - **A stale "needs you" is no longer checked by reading the transcript on the interface thread.** The check that clears a permission prompt Claude already answered elsewhere ran while Perch was drawing, and read up to 256 KB each time the transcript changed. It now runs alongside the scan, and a prompt raised again in the meantime keeps its "needs you" until the scan has looked.
### Improved - **Less work on an idle Mac.** With no phone or watch connected, Perch no longer asks tmux, Herdr or OpenCode every four seconds whether each session can be typed into — nothing reads the answer until a companion connects, and the first one to connect triggers a fresh check. Two Claude sessions in the same repo also share one directory read per scan instead of two. - **OpenCode sessions with long histories cost less per scan.** Perch read every message in a session to find the newest one; it now asks the database for just that message when the session already carries its own totals.
